1 Court No. - 80  HON'BLE RAJEEV MISRA, J. 
Ref:
On Appeal 1.
Heard Mr. Dharmendra Kumar Gupta, the learned counsel for appellants and the learned AGA for State.

2. Admit.3. Summon the lower court record.
4.

Notice on behalf of State/opposite party-1 has been accepted by the learned A.G.A.
5.
List this appeal for hearing in due course.
Ref: Order on Application for Suspension of Sentence 1.
Heard Mr. Dharmendra Kumar Gupta, the learned counsel for applicants/appellant and the learned AGA for State.

2. Perused the record.
3.

Feeling aggrieved by the judgement and order dated 16.7.2025, passed by Additional District/Sessions Judge/Fast Track Court No. 1, Bareilly in Sessions Trial No. 781 of 2023 (State Vs.
Avsar @ Afsar and 2 Others) under sections 504 506 IPC, Police Station- Faridpur, District- Bareilly applicants/appellant has approached this Court by filing aforementioned criminal appeal.

sentences.text: 4. By means of impugned judgement and order, applicants/appellants have been convicted under section 504 IPC therefore sentenced to one year rigorous imprisonment, along with fine of Rs.5,000/- and in case of default in payment of fine, applicants/appellants are to undergo one month additional imprisonment, under section 506 IPC therefore sentenced to one year rigorous imprisonment, along with fine of Rs.5,000/- and

in case of default in payment of fine,
applicants/appellants are to undergo one month additional simple imprisonment.
Co-accused Avsar @ Afsar has been convicted and sentenced under section 376, 452, 504, 506 IPC.
The impugned judgement and order further records that both the sentences shall run concurrently.
5. Learned counsel for applicants/appellants submits that applicants/appellants were enlarged on bail during the pendency of trial.
However, subsequent to the impugned judgment and order dated 16.7.2025 passed by court below applicants/appellants were taken into custody.

However, as sentence awarded to applicants/appellants by Court below under the impugned judgement and Iqrar And Another vs State Of U.P. on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34835799/
2 order is one year, therefore, applicants/appellants filed an application for interim bail as provided under Section 389 (3) Cr.P.C./430(i) BNSS.

entities.text: Iqrar And Another vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The same was allowed by Court below vide order dated 16.7.2025.
Copy of said order is on record and has been appended at page 141 of the paper book.
However, interim bail granted to applicants/appellants by Court below is for a limited period i.e. for the period of limitation provided for filing an appeal.
Accordingly, applicants/appellants have filed above mentioned application for suspension of sentence/grant of bail seeking their enlargement on bail during the pendency of present appeal.

6. Mr. Dharmendra Kumar Gupta, the learned counsel for applicants/appellants, in support of the application for suspension of sentence/prayer for bail, submits that even though applicants/appellants are named as well as convicted accused however, irrespective of above but in view of the facts as have now crystalized on record, applicants/appellants are liable to be enlarged on bail during the pendency of present appeal.
7. In furtherance of aforesaid submission, the learned counsel for applicants/appellants submits that applicants/appellants were enlarged on bail during the pendency of trial.
However, there is nothing on record to show that applicants/appellants misused the liberty of bail.

As such,
applicants/appellants are liable to be enlarged on bail during the pendency of present appeal also.

8. According to the learned counsel for applicants/appellants sentence awarded by Court below against applicants/appellants is a definite sentence/punishment, inasmuch as the maximum sentence awarded to applicants/appellants by Court below is one year.

However, in view of heavy pendency of criminal appeals before this Court coupled with the fact that there is an acute shortage of Hon'ble Judges in this Court, therefore there is no likelihood of the present appeal being heard in near future.

On the aforesaid premise, the learned counsel for applicants/appellants submits that in view of aforementioned peculiar and precarious circumstance, resulting in uncertainty in the hearing of present appeal, applicants/appellants are liable to be enlarged on bail during the pendency of present appeal.

9. To buttress his submission the learned counsel for applicants/appellants referred to the judgement of Supreme Court in Atul @ Ashutosh Vs. State of M.P., (2024) 3 SCC 663 wherein the Apex Court has itself observed that where definite sentence, punishment has been awarded by Court below against an accused and there is no possibility of the appeal being heard in near future, then in such a circumstances the appellate Court must enlarge such a convict on bail during the pendency of appeal.
10.

entities.text: Atul @ Ashutosh Vs. State of M.P., (2024) 3 SCC 663
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: According to the learned counsel for applicants/appellants there does not exist any such distinguishing feature in the case of present applicants/appellants on the basis of which the ratio laid down by Apex Court in aforementioned judgment can be so distinguished so as to deny bail to applicants/appellants, during the pendency of present appeal.
He, therefore contends that in view of above and also the aforementioned judgement of Supreme Court, applicant/appellant is liable to be enlarged on bail during the pendency of present appeal.

sentences.text: 3 11. Even otherwise, applicants/appellants are men of clean antecedents inasmuch as they have no criminal history to their credit except the present one.

In view of above, the uncertainty in the hearing of present appeal, in near future the fact that applicants/appellants were enlarged on bail during the pendency of trial, but there is nothing on record to show that applicants/appellants misused the liberty of bail, and there being no such compelling circumstance on record, warranting custodial arrest of applicants/appellants during the pendency of present appeal
, learned counsel for applicants/appellants would thus submit that applicants/appellants are liable to be enlarged on bail during the pendency of present appeal.
In case the applicants/appellants are enlarged on bail, then in that eventuality they shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate in the hearing of present appeal.
12. Per contra, the learned A.G.A. representing State-opposite party-1 has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail.
He submits that since applicants/appellants are named as well as and convicted accused, and under incarceration, therefore, they do not deserve any indulgence by this Court.

Learned A.G.A. submits that co-accused has been convicted for an offence under section 376 IPC,
applicants are thus claiming parity to a crime which is not only illegal but immoral but also henious.
As such, no illegality or perversity have been attached to applicants/appellants.

On the aforesaid conspectus, the learned A.G.A. contends that interest of justice shall better be served in case the appeal itself is heard finally by fixing a short date rather than enlarging the applicants/appellants on bail during the pendency of appeal.

However, the learned A.G.A. could not dislodge the factual and legal submissions urged by the learned counsel for applicants/appellants, in support of the applicaiton for suspension of sentence with reference to the record at this stage.

13. Having heard the learned counsel for applicants/appellants, the learned A.G.A. for State, upon perusal of material brought on record, evidence, nature and gravity of offence as well as complicity of applicants/appellants, accusation made this Court finds that applicants/appellants are named as well as convicted accused, applicants/appellants were enlarged on bail during the pendency of trial,
however, there is noting on record to show that applicants/appellant misused the liberty of bail,
applicants/appellants have been sentenced to 1 year maximum sentence, by court below, as such sentence awarded by Court below to applicants-appellants is a definite sentence punishment,
however, in view of heavy pendency of criminal appeals before this Court and also an acute shortage of Hon'ble Judges in this Court, there is no likelihood of the present appeal being heard in near future, as such, in view of aforementioned peculiar and precarious circumstance, there is uncertainty in the hearing of present appeal in near future, as such, prima facie applicants/appellants are liable to be to be enlarged on bail, during the pendency of present appeal,
Apex Court in the case of Atul @ Ashutosh (Supra) has itself observed that where sentence awarded to a convict by court below is a definite sentence punishment and there are no chances of the appeal being heard in near future, then in such a circumstance such a convict should be enlarged on bail during the pendency of appeal, the learned A.G.A. could not point out any such distinguishing feature from the record so as to distinguish aforementioned judgement and deny bail to applicants/appellants, the clean antecedents of applicants/appellants inasmuch as they have no criminal history to their credit, except the present one, no such incriminating circumstance has emerged on record so as to warrant custodial arrest of applicants/appellants during the pendency of present appeal, therefore, considering the above and irrespective of the objections raised by the Iqrar And Another vs State Of U.P. on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34835799/
4 learned A.G.A. in opposition to this application for suspension of sentence, but without making any comment on the merits of the appeal, this Court finds that applicants/appellants have made out a case for bail.
14.

sentences.text: As such, the application for suspension of sentence succeeds and is liable to be allowed.
15. It is, accordingly, allowed.

16. The interim bail granted to applicants-appellant- Iqrar and Nishar by Court below are, hereby,
made absolute.

17. It is, however, provided that the amount of fine awarded by court below, if not deposited, shall be deposited by applicants-appellant with the Court below within a period of 1 month from today failing which, the bail granted to applicants-appellant under this order shall stand canceled and they shall be taken into custody at once to serve out the sentence awarded by Court below.
Rajeev Misra,J.) September 4, 2025
